title: The Ghost of Tashkent
premise: Freya Oyelaran, a crash investigator who lost her family in an unexplained accident, has built a career on cases nobody wants to claim. When her long-dead intelligence handler emails her a meeting invitation, she is pulled into a conspiracy: a staged air disaster designed to bury evidence of a black-site operation she once unknowingly serviced. Racing across Tashkent and London with a defector who knows too much, Freya must decide whether justice means exposing the truth or becoming the ghost she was trained to be. In the end she grounds the attack by sacrificing her anonymity, testifying publicly at devastating personal cost, and finally claiming both her grief and her name.
about_author: Isandro Brightwater is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports no one read. He now writes thrillers about the people who read them anyway.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash that killed her family, Freya works a routine wreckage case in Tashkent, methodical and emotionally walled-off. Her handler, Marek, whom she buried three years ago, sends her a calendar invite for tomorrow, 6 a.m., with coordinates she recognizes from row twelve's flight path. Beat: dread cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She verifies the email's cryptographic signature: genuinely Marek's, dated after his death. At the meeting site she finds only a dead drop containing a burner phone and a partial manifest proving the crash that killed her family carried undeclared cargo. Beat: the personal becomes professional; suspicion ignites into purpose.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intercut with the antagonist Voss, a fixer who erases inconvenient accidents. Freya traces the cargo to a shell company tied to a pending flight, AZ-447, scheduled in nine days. Voss learns someone is pulling threads. Beat: the hunter realizes she is also hunted.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She extracts Yusuf Karimov, a frightened former logistics clerk whose testimony could stop AZ-447 but who trusts no institution. A safehouse ambush forces them to flee together through Tashkent's night markets. Beat: reluctant alliance; Freya feels belonging stir where she least wants it.

chapters.title: What Marek Knew
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. Decoding Marek's dead-drop files, Yusuf reveals the pattern: a series of 'accidents' all covering the same black-site supply chain, and Freya's family crash among them. Freya breaks down privately, then hardens. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the theme of justice outside the law sharpens.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They reach London to find allies are compromised; her old agency offers protection in exchange for silence about the chain. Voss frames Freya for a colleague's murder, making her officially invisible, exactly as she always pretended to be. Beat: isolation weaponized; the cost of invisibility made literal.

chapters.title: The Ghost Who Wouldn't Stay
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss hunts Freya using her own investigative habits against her, predicting her moves from her case files. But his model fails because he can't account for her choosing risk for another person, shielding Yusuf. Beat: villain's confidence curdles; humanity as the unquantifiable variable.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. With two days left, Freya infiltrates the charter operator behind AZ-447 and finds the sabotage already installed. To ground the flight legally she must expose evidence she swore to bury, including proof implicating her own past work. Beat: climax of choice; identity versus safety.

chapters.title: AZ-447
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, real-time tension. The flight boards; Freya triggers the grounding while Voss tries to force departure, culminating in a confrontation on the tarmac where she chooses arrest over killing him, forcing witnesses and cameras to see everything. Beat: climax; justice performed in daylight, not shadow.

chapters.title: Named
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue months later. Testifying before an inquiry, Freya speaks her family's names aloud for the first time in years, the supply chain exposed, Marek's posthumous plan fulfilled. She takes a teaching post training honest investigators, no longer hiding. Beat: resolution; belonging earned through truth rather than anonymity.
